questions.question: Alluri Sitaram Raju was a tribal freedom fighter from which state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

About Alluri Sitaram Raju:

__
 
• In 1922, Indian revolutionary Alluri Sitaram Raju led the Rampa Rebellion against the British raj for their imposition of the 1882 Madras Forest Act, which severely restricted the free movement of the tribal community within their own forests.
 
• Under the implications of this Act, the community was unable to fully carry out the traditional Podu agricultural system, which involved shifting cultivation.
 
• The armed struggle came to a violent end in 1924, when Raju was captured by police forces, tied to a tree, and shot by a firing squad. His heroics resulted in him being titled manyam veerudu, or ‘the hero of the jungle’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Komaram Bheem:

 
• Born in Telangana’s Adilabad district in 1901, Bheem was a member of the Gond community and grew up in the populated forests of the Chanda and Ballalpur kingdoms.
 
• Komaram Bheem had escaped from prison to a tea plantation in Assam.
 
• Here, he heard about the rebellion being led by Alluri and found a new sense of inspiration to protect the Gond tribe to which he belonged.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations issues one rupee currency notes and coins in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Ministry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Finance** is responsible for producing the **one rupee note and coins.**
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** has exclusive jurisdiction to issue** currency notes** of **various denominations,** with the exception of notes of one rupee, according to **Section 22 of the Reserve Bank of India Act.**
 
• The o**ne rupee note and coins, **which include the **Finance Secretary's signature,** are distributed by the Ministry of Finance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Imperial Bank Of India:**

 
 
• On **January 27, 1921**, the Imperial Bank of India was founded.
 
• **Bengal, Bombay, and Madras presidency banks** have been combined into this bank.
 
• With India's independence, it changed its name to the **State Bank of India.**
 
 
 
• **Industrial Finance Corporation of India:**
 
 
• **In 1948**, IFCI Ltd was established as a **Statutory Company** with the goal of offering industry medium- and long-term financing.
 
• After the **Industrial Finance Corporation Act** was repealed in 1993, IFCI was incorporated as a **public limited company **and registered under the **Companies Act of 1956.**
 
• IFCI is listed as a **Systemically Important Non-Deposit **Taking **Non-Banking Financial Corporation** with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 
 
 
 
• **Central Bank of India**:
 
 
• An Indian public sector bank with its headquarters in **Mumbai** is the Central Bank of India.
 
• The **Banking Companies (Acquisition & Transfer of Undertakings) Act** of **1970** founded it.

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the largest atomic radii?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lithium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atomic radii are the distance between the nucleus of an atom and the outermost orbit of an electron.**

 
 
• It is measured in nanometers (nm) or picometers (pm)
 
• It can be measured using X-ray or any spectroscopic method.
 
 
 
• In the periodic table, as we move **from left to right, the atomic radii decrease.**
 
• **Among Beryllium, Lithium, Nitrogen, and Carbon, Lithium has the highest atomic radius with 152 pm. Hence option 2 is correct.**
 
 
• Followed by Beryllium (111 pm), Carbon (77 pm), and Nitrogen (74 pm).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The atomic radii decrease and when we go down a group, they increase. **

 
 
• In this trend, **Sodium has bigger atomic radii (186 pm) than Lithium, followed by Potassium (231 pm).**
 
 
 
• **Beryllium** is a greyish steel metal that is brittle at a bottom temperature that is used for industrial purposes like **Aircraft Braking systems, Satellites, Ceramic manufacture etc.**
 
• **Lithium **is a soft and silver metal used in **batteries, digital cameras, laptops etc.**
 
• **Nitrogen **is a colourless and odourless element used in **manufacturing fertilizers, nylon, dyes etc.**
 
• **Carbon **is a nonmetal and is used in **metal smelting**, and impure carbon is in the form of charcoal which is **used for cooking** and in the industrial water treatment process.

questions.question: Who won a gold medal for India in the javelin throw event at Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neeraj Chopra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Neeraj Chopra

__
 
• Neeraj Chopra is originally from Khandala village in Panipat, Haryana. 
 
• He was born on 24 December 1997. His father Satish Kumar is a farmer.
 
• Neeraj Chopra is an Indian Track and field athlete and a Junior Commissioned Officer in Indian Army.
 
• The distance reached by the javelin in the gold medal-winning throw by Neeraj Chopra at the Olympic games held in Tokyo in 2021 lay between 87.5 m and 88.0 m.
 
• Tokyo Olympics: India's Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal in the men's javelin throw event with a throw of 87.58m in his second attempt.
 
• Neeraj is the first Indian in over 120 years, and the first athlete from independent India, to win an Olympic medal in a track-and-field discipline.
 
• Chopra also became the sixth Indian athlete to win an individual medal at Tokyo 2020 joining weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, shuttler PV Sindhu, boxer Lovlina Borgohain, and wrestlers Ravi Kumar Dahiya and Bajrang Punia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At the Gold Coast Commonwealth Games, Neeraj threw an 86.47-meter spear and won the gold medal.
 
• India's star javelin throwing athlete Neeraj Chopra threw the javelin 88.07 meters away in the fifth attempt.
 
• It Breached the national record of 88.06 meters to win the gold medal in the 2018 Asian Games.
 
• Parsa Singh of India won the silver medal in the first Asian Games (1951) played in Delhi.
 
• After this, in the 1982 Asian Games (Delhi), India's Gurtej Singh won the bronze medal.
 
• So far no athlete had achieved a gold medal in the javelin throw, but Neeraj Chopra made the best-ever performance for India in the javelin throw.

questions.question: In which type of Megalith (grave/memorial) were the stone pieces set in a circular shape around the grave?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cairn circle.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• A **megalith** is a** big prehistoric stone** that has been utilized, either** alone or in conjunction **with other stones, to build a **structure or monument.**
 
• The** prehistoric stone row, or cairn-circles**, is a straight line of** parallel megalithic **standing stones.
 
• **250 cairn circles** have recently been identified by the **State Department of Archaeology **in **Chennai **from the **Kodumanal excavation site** in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The discovery of **10 pots and bowls **from the site, which were positioned outside of **three-chambered burial cists** and inside the cairn circle, is a first.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dolmen:**

 
 
• A dolmen or** portal tomb** is a form of the **single-chamber megalithic tomb,** usually consisting of two or more upright megaliths supporting a massive flat **horizontal capstone or "table".**
 
 
 
• **Rock cut cave:**
 
 
• A kind of rock art known as rock-cut architecture involves carving a building out of a** piece of solid, uncut rock.**
 
 
 
• **Menhir:**
 
 
• A menhir is a **huge upright stone **that was set in the ground by humans and is thought to have originated in **Europe during** the** middle Bronze Age.**

• **H**e was one of the **Navaratnas.**

• **Birbal** served as the **main army commander** at the court of Mughal emperor Akbar.

questions.question: The feature of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** authors of the Constitution** took inspiration from othe**r international constitutions** for a number of its aspects.
 
• The** American Constitution** served as a template for **India's Fundamental Rights.**
 
• Other significant elements, such as the **Written Constitution, the President's role **as the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, and others, are drawn from the constitutions of other nations.
 
• **Fundamental rights** are** basic rights** provided to the people in order to live with **dignity and integrity.**
 
• They are protected by the **Indian Constitution's Part III.**
 
• Other elements taken from the **US constitution include**
 
 
• an independent judiciary and judicial review,
 
• impeachment of the president,
 
• removal of justices from the Supreme Court and High Court, and
 
• the Vice-presidential position.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elements taken from the Australian constitution include:**

 
 
• Concurrent list
 
• Freedom of trade
 
• Commerce and intercourse
 
• Joint sitting of the Upper and Lower House.
 
 
 
• **Elements taken from the British constitution include:**
 
 
• Parliamentary form of Government
 
• Rule of law
 
• Legislative procedure
 
• Single Citizenship
 
• Cabinet system
 
• Prerogative writs
 
• Bicameralism
 
 
 
• **Elements taken from the Ireland constitution include:**
 
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy
 
• Nomination of Rajya Sabha members
 
• Method of election of the President

questions.question: Sundari trees are found in the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **species of mangrove tree **found in the **Malvaceae family** is called ***Heritiera fomes*__. **
 
• **Sunder, sundri, jekanazo, and pinlekanazo** are some of its common names.
 
• It makes up around **70% of the trees **in the **Sundarbans of Bangladesh and India** and is the main type of mangrove tree there.
 
• **__*H. fomes*__** is a significant tree that** produces lumber.**
 
• The Sundari tree can be found in the **Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.**
 
• They are also known as the **Sunderbans** due to the large number of these trees in those areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahanadi delta:**

 
 
• **Mangroves and** their allies are found in great variety in the Mahanadi delta, which includes the districts of** Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, and Puri.**
 
• It is situated on India's east coast in the state of **Odisha.**
 
 
 
• **Godavari delta:**
 
 
• The States of **Telangana, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh **make up this interstate subbasin.
 
• **Avicennia, Suaeda, Rhizophora, and Bruguiera species** are among the distinguishing trees; they are the **typical genera of Asia-Pacific mangroves.**
 
 
 
• **Muthupet delta:**
 
 
• In the southernmost tip of the **Cauvery river delta**, on the Gulf of Bengal, is** Muthupet Lagoon.**
 
• This beautiful area is usually green thanks to the **mangrove vegetation. **

questions.question: The number of females per 1000 males in the population is called the ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sex ratio.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The sex ratio** is defined as the **number of females per 1000 males** in a given population.
 
• In a society where the **number of males and females is equal,** there are **1000 females for every 1000 males** or a **1:1 sex ratio.**
 
• According to **National Family Health Survey, **2020-21 (NFHS-5) India's Sex ratio in 2022 is **1020 females per 1000 males.**
 
• The sex ratio is **1037 in rural areas** and** 985 females for every 1000 males** in **urban areas.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **birth rate:**

 
 
• The** number of babies born** in a population in a** specific period of time **is known as the birth rate.
 
 
 
• **death rate:**
 
 
• **A population's mortality rate**, often known as the death rate, is a **measurement of the number of deaths** within that population per unit of time, scaled to that **population's size.**
 
 
 
• **literacy rate:**
 
 
• The literacy rate is calculated by dividing the population of **adults aged 7 and older **who are literate by the total population of adults in the same age group.

questions.question: ______ includes all non-living components, such as air, cloud, dust, land, mountains, rivers, temperature, humidity, water, water vapour, sand, etc.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abiotic environment.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• All of an **ecosystem's nonliving components** and processes are referred to as its **abiotic environment.**
 
• Examples of significant **abiotic variables **that interact with one another and have an impact on** living things, **such as plants and animals, are **sunlight, soil, water, wind, and humidity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biotic environment:**

 
 
• **Living things** that influence other** living things **either **directly or indirectly** reside in an abiotic environment.
 
• A biotic factor is a** living creature **that modifies its environment.
 
 
 
• **Artificial environment:**
 
 
• **A simulation model's operating environment** is represented by an artificial environment.
 
 
 
• **Healthy environment:**
 
 
• A **safe food and water supply, adequate waste disposal, clean air, and the absence of pests** like flies, cockroaches, and mosquitoes are all characteristics of a clean and healthy environment.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters of India revived the Indian National Army ‘Azad Hind Fauj’ (which was formed in 1942 by Rash Behari Bose and Captain-General Mohan Singh) in the year 1943?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Subhas Chandra Bose__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Azad Hind Fauj or the India National Army (INA) was first established by Mohan Singh in 1942.

 
 
• It was revived by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose on October 21, 1943, during the Second World War to secure India’s complete independence from British Raj.
 
• On this day, India’s first independent provisional government named Azad Hind Government was announced.
 
• This was followed by a conference in Bangkok (June 1942), where Rashbehari Bose was elected president of the league and a decision was taken to raise the Indian National Army.
 
• Captain Mohan Singh was appointed the commander of the INA, which had about 40,000 Indian soldiers
 
• This conference invited Bose to lead the movement.
 
 
• Earlier, Bose had escaped from India in 1941 to Berlin.
 
• In June 1943 he came to Tokyo and then India joined the INA in Singapore.
 
 
 
• Rashbehari Bose handed over the leadership to Subhas Bose, and an Azad Hind Sarkar was formed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:**

 
 
• **​**He was born on 2 October 1869.
 
• He started his political career in South Africa where he launched a Civil Disobedience Movement against the maltreatment meted out to Asian settlers.
 
• In 1915, he returned to India and took up the leadership of the National Freedom Struggle.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi led the national freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• Gandhiji launched many movements to force the British to concede India its Independence.
 
• The well-known being is Non-Co-operation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), and the Quit India Movement (1942).
 
• Gandhi wrote his famous autobiography under the title 'My Experiments with Truth'.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi is better known as the father of the Nation.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of free India between 15 August 1947 – 27 May 1964.
 
• He was also one of the principal leaders of India’s independence movement in the 1930s and ’40s.
 
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh:**
 
 
• **​**Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were involved in the Lahore conspiracy case and because of this, the court had ordered that they were to be hanged on March 23, 1931.
 
• March 23 was the day of execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru is observed as the Shaheed Diwas in India every year so as a show of respect for its revolutionary heroes.
 
• Three of them were involved in the killing of John Saunders, a British cop who was believed to have thrashed Lala Lajpatpat Rai.
 
• They were members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
 
• Bhagat Singh along with Batukeshwar Dutt threw a harmless bomb in the Central Legislative assembly to protest the passing of the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.
 
• Bhagat Singh popularized the phrase " Inqualab Zindabad" which was first phrased by Maulana Hazrat Mohani.
 
• Some of the books written by Bhagat Singh are "Why I Am an Atheist", "No Hanging, Please Shoot Us", "on the Path of Liberation" among others.

questions.question: Sattriya is a classical dance form of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Assam__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Satriya Nritya is the classical dance form of Assam which represents the Satriya culture, the basis of the religious and cultural fabric of Assam__.

 __
 
• It is a dance-drama performance art with origins in the Krishna-centered Vaishnavism monasteries of Assam and attributed to the 15th-century Bhakti movement scholar and saint Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev.
 
• Dance historian Dr. Sunil Kothari has recently been bestowed with the Madhabdev Award by the Government of Assam for popularising Sattriya dance.
 
• Sattriya was given the status of classical dance in the year 2000 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers of India drains into the Bay of Bengal?
questions.solution:

__

• It flows through Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **It forms a delta in Andhra Pradesh and finally drains into the Bay of Bengal. Hence option 2 is correct.**

• **It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and drains into the Gulf of Cambay in the Arabian Sea.**
 
• **Narmada river is a west flowing river that originates at Amarkantak range in the Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat and **drains into the Gulf of Cambay in the Arabian Sea.**
 
• **Mahi river originates in Dhar district in Madhya Pradesh** and flows through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat and finally **drains into the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea.**

questions.question: Who among the following Indian dancers was the first woman in Indian history to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Parliamentary form of government consists of three parts: The president, The Rajya Sabha (Council of States or the upper house) and the Lok Sabha (House of People or the lower house).
 
• The Rajya Sabha has a fixed 250 members of maximum out of which **238 are the representatives of the states and UTs elected indirectly** and 12 are nominated by the president.
 
• **Classical Bharatnatyam dancer from Tamil Nadu, Rukmini Devi Arundale became the first woman in India to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha in 1952. Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
 
• **​She was honoured with Padma Bhushan in 1956** and Sangeet Natak Academy Fellowship in 1967.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• ​She has featured in Forbes India's Celebrities 100 list and was **honoured with Padma Sri in 2008.**
 
 
 
• **Mallika Sarabhai is an Indian classical dancer in Kuchipudi and Bharatnatyam** from Gujarat and is the daughter of classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai and Vikram Sarabhai, who is considered a father of Indian Space program.
 
 
• **​In 2010, she was honoured with Padma Bhushan**.
 
 
 
• **Saroj Khan was an Indian dancer and choreographer** who worked in Hindi films and was the **first to be honoured with Filmfare best choreography award.**
 
• Currently, there are 245 members of the Rajya Sabha out of which 229 members represent the states.
 
• The representatives of states are elected by the elected members of the state legislative assembly and the representatives of UTs are indirectly elected by the members of the electoral college of the UT.

questions.question: The steep rocky coast rising almost vertically above sea water is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sea cliff**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A cliff is a hard rock that rises very high vertically and these landscapes are formed near the seas or oceans.**
 
• They are formed due to erosion and weathering.
 
 
• **The cliff formed near a sea is called a Sea cliff and these are steep faces of rock. Hence option 2 is correct.**
 
 
 
• These are formed by destructive waves (created by coastal erosion) with high energy crashing against the coastline until a notch is formed. 
 
• **Sea Cliffs of Molokai in Hawaii are the tallest sea cliffs in the world which rose to 3000 feet above sea level.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sea caves are a type of cave formed when cracks in rocks at the cliff's base are eroded (primary erosion) and expanded by the sea waves.**
 
• Examples of sea caves are Fingal's cave in Scotland, Papanikolis cave in Greece and Smoo cave in Scotland.
 
• **Sea arches are natural bridges formed when a cave continues to be eroded and expanded due to the forces of water erosion until it cuts through its headland.**
 
• **Ox-bow lake is a U-shaped lake formed when a meander is cut off forming a free body of water.**
 
 
• In Amazon, ox-bow lakes are very common and provide habitat to wildlife.
